thm:GT-relation-valued-limit.title: Relation-valued compactness and tracewise weak closure
thm:GT-relation-valued-limit.note: TRIAGE V047 (2026-08-21): Hard — finite/library-scale. Requires a new reusable finite-dimensional/library component, a large model-specific assembly, or a multi-module compiler. MACHINERY (2026-08-22): RelationValuedLimitExact.lean proves the defect-closure clause exactly: for nonempty compact graphs Gamma_n converging in Hausdorff distance to a nonempty compact Gamma (TR.7) and continuous nonnegative defects d_{j,n} converging uniformly to d_j with sup_{Gamma_n} d_{j,n} -> 0 (TR.8), every point of Gamma is a limit of points of Gamma_n (exists_approx, via exists_dist_lt_of_hausdorffDist_lt') and d_j = 0 on Gamma (defect_eq_zero_on_limit). The single-valued clause is proved under the equicontinuous-fibre hypothesis EquicontinuousFibres (for every eps there is delta with dist(y,y') < eps whenever (x,y),(x',y') in Gamma_n, dist(x,x') < delta, for all large n): the limit relation then has a uniform modulus (limit_modulus), its fibres are singletons and it is the graph of a continuous response on its domain (limit_is_graph). FIDELITY REMARK: the literal hypothesis (TR.9) sup_x diam Gamma_n(x) -> 0 is not sufficient for the stated conclusion: the graphs of x -> clamp(n x) on [-1,1] have singleton fibres for every n but converge in Hausdorff distance to a set containing the vertical segment {0} x [0,1]; a fibre-equicontinuity condition across neighbouring base points (as in the Lean EquicontinuousFibres) is needed. Status remains conditional_interface because the Lean single-valued clause uses this strengthened hypothesis. TRIAGE-EXACT: HARD - Literal (TR.9) clause refuted by clamp counterexample; provable only under strengthened equicontinuity.
